summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his detailed analysis of the Prophet Muhammad's prayer (salah), focusing on the specifics of Quranic recitation during different prayer positions. He discusses which of the five obligatory prayers involve audible versus silent recitation, the practice of making the last two units (rakahs) shorter than the first two (approximately half their length), and the Prophet's sunnah of sometimes reciting only Surah Al-Fatihah in the final rakahs. Sh. Ali Mashhour clarifies the three pauses that occur during the standing position in prayer and their purposes, particularly addressing common misconceptions about whether followers behind the imam should recite Surah Al-Fatihah during the imam's silence.
